one_session_per_proof.name: one sealed session per token proof

steps.step: unsealed hello: insecure, the nonces untouched
an update carrying access_expires_at: kept with the pair
an update without it: the stored one is cleared
a duplicate access_expires_at: invalid_value, nothing stored
a space before the object (the first byte must be '{'): invalid_value, nothing stored

sealed_data.name: sealed data in a sealed session
sealed_data.note: This receiver keeps the session after a refusal to show the counter rules; a device may end it instead, and a client stops using a session after any refusal (re-prove, one sealed hello).

steps.step: client: data, the VM's answer (counter 0, 4 writes)
client: unsealed data in a sealed session: refused
client: data counter 3, first write then abort
client: data counter 5 with a bad tag: refused, counter not used
client: the real data counter 5: accepted

sealed_interleaved.name: two sealed messages in flight, the earlier refused at its tag

steps.step: data counter 1, whole, while the update is in flight
the rest of the update: refused at its tag, counter 0 left open once
the real update counter 0: accepted (the hole)
the real update counter 0 replayed: refused

receiver_limits.name: the receiver's limits (client to device)
receiver_limits.note: Each case is a session of its own (its nonces), the receiver's counter from 0; a step's outcome is its last frame's. A refusal before the counter is taken leaves it for the next message; one after it (a malformed fragment) uses it, like an abort.

cases.name: a first write without the whole counter

steps.step: data counter 0, its first write with 3 of the counter's 4 bytes: invalid_length, the counter not taken
data counter 0, its first write with total_len 4097 (over max_message 4096): invalid_value, the counter not taken
data counter 0 with no plaintext, total_len 20: invalid_value, the counter not taken

cases.name: a write marked last short of total_len

steps.step: data counter 0 in one write marked last, total_len 5 more than it carries: invalid_value, the counter used
the rest with one byte past total_len: invalid_value, the counter used

cases.name: a first write while a message is open

steps.step: data counter 1, a first write while counter 0's is open: invalid_value, both dropped, counter 1 not taken

cases.name: a continuation without the sealed flag

steps.step: the rest without the sealed flag: invalid_value, the counter used

cases.name: a hole more than 255 counters back

steps.step: credentials_update counter 0 (bad tag): its first write
data counters 1 to 254, one write each: each accepted
the rest of the update: refused at its tag, counter 0 left open once (255 back)
data counter 255: accepted; counter 0 is now 256 back, so it closes
the real update counter 0: refused (no hole any more)

sealed_credentials_saved.name: sealed credentials_saved
sealed_credentials_saved.note: Plaintext = result || SHA-256(refresh_token)[:8] (zeros when not saved), sealed under the next device-to-client counter and fragmented as data in one write. The client counts only a sealed [1] with the matching hash as saved; with no sealed answer within 35 s while the link stays up it assumes saved (older firmware answers unsealed); a dropped link keeps the pair pending.

steps.step: saved: sealed [1] with the hash of this pair
not saved: sealed [0] (also a deferred write-back that gave up)
a sealed [1] with another pair's hash: not saved
an unsealed [1] confirms nothing and uses no counter; the sealed [1] after it decides
an unsealed [0]: not saved (it can only cause a resend)

sealed_data_large.name: sealed data in a sealed session, with a sealed credentials_saved
sealed_data_large.note: This receiver keeps the session after a refusal to show the counter rules; a device may end it instead, and a client stops using a session after any refusal (re-prove, one sealed hello).

steps.step: client: data, the VM's answer (counter 0, 4 writes)
client: unsealed data in a sealed session: refused
client: data counter 3, first write then abort
client: data counter 5 with a bad tag: refused, counter not used
client: the real data counter 5: accepted

sealed_stream_restart.name: the VM stream restarted in the same sealed session after a message cut by an error

steps.step: device: data (counter 2), its first write only: an error ends the VM stream
device: open_request [0]: only the stream ends, the sealed session stays
client: credentials_update (counter 1) while the stream ends: saved, its answer held
client: state closed (epoch 1): the cut message is dropped, its counter used
device: credentials_saved, sealed (counter 3), after the state
device: open_request [1] at once: the stream asked for again
client: state open (epoch 2): the same sealed session
device: data, the new stream's link.register (counter 4)

relabelled.name: a sealed message relabelled: seal v1's tag doesn't cover the sub-command
relabelled.note: Current behaviour, not a wire change: the relabelled frame differs from the sent one in its sub-command byte alone, unseals under the same counter and tag, and its plaintext is valid for the label it arrives under. Seal v2 binds the sub-command and the session epoch into the tag. The plaintexts are the VM's choice and not ServiceResponseEnvelopes: a device that takes a sent frame as data refuses it (sent_as_data: error invalid_value, its counter used); only the relabel gets them taken.

steps.step: one byte 0x00 as data, relabelled clear: the gadget erases its tokens
a JSON object as data, relabelled credentials_update: the stored pair is replaced

description: Sealed device-session credentials (mgcommands.h, Sealed credentials). enc_key||mac_key = HKDF-SHA256(salt, K, client_nonce||device_nonce||node_id, 64); keystream block i = HMAC-SHA256(enc_key, stream_label||dir||counter_be32||i_be32); tag = HMAC-SHA256(mac_key, tag_label||dir||counter_be32||len_be32||ciphertext)[:16]; sealed = counter_be32||ciphertext||tag. dir 1 = device->client, 2 = client->device. One sealed session per token proof: a second sealed hello under the same proof is refused with error [session, proof_required] (one_session_per_proof). access_expires_at: a device that keeps it stores an update's positive integer with the pair (any other form: none; an update without it clears it; a duplicate is invalid_value) and hands it back last in its next credentials (access_expires_at: the sealed steps over three proofs, with the device's answer and what it keeps). sealed_data: in a sealed session every message with a payload (credentials, credentials_update, data) is sealed whole and then fragmented (total_len counts sealed bytes), one counter per direction shared by all of them, the counter read from the first fragment (next only; an aborted message uses its counter, a message refused at its tag does not); a replayed counter or a bad tag is refused with invalid_value, unsealed data with insecure. sealed_interleaved: two sealed messages in flight together; the earlier one refused at its tag after a later counter was taken leaves that counter open once (a hole). receiver_limits: what the receiver refuses (a first fragment without the whole counter, total_len of 20 or less or over max_message, fragments that don't add up to total_len or lose the sealed flag, a first fragment while one is open, a hole over 255 back) and what each does to the counter. sealed_credentials_saved: in a sealed session the device's credentials_saved is sealed too (plaintext: result || SHA-256(refresh_token)[:8], zeros when not saved); the client counts only a sealed [1] with the matching hash as saved, an unsealed [1] confirms nothing, and with no sealed answer in 35 s of link it assumes saved. The access_expires_at steps test the storage rule and keep the legacy one-byte answer; the sealed answer is in sealed_credentials_saved. sealed_data_large: sealed_data as a device that seals credentials_saved (mg_session_hello_flag_sealed_saved) sends it (its sealed credentials_saved takes device counter 2, so its later data is counter 3); an implementation that seals credentials_saved replays sealed_data_large, one that doesn't sealed_data. sealed_stream_restart: an error ends only the VM stream (open_request [0], the client's closed, open_request [1], open) in the same sealed session; a device message cut after its first fragment used its counter on both sides, a sealed credentials_saved owed meanwhile goes after the state that cuts it off, and the next sealed message each way unseals at the next counter. Client data plaintexts are ServiceResponseEnvelopes (a body chunk on stream 3 carrying stand-in bytes), which a device decodes first; client data that isn't one is refused invalid_value, its counter used. relabelled: what seal v1 doesn't cover - the tag is over dir, counter and ciphertext, not the sub-command byte, so the same sealed bytes under another sub-command still unseal and the plaintext parses there (0x00 as a clear, a JSON object as a credentials_update).
